課程概述:
本課程著重於生醫工程領域中常用之生理訊號量測、訊號處理與應用開發，旨在培養學生具備跨領域的工程實務能力與醫療健康科技應用視野。課程內容涵蓋 EEG（腦電圖）、ECG（心電圖）、EMG（肌電圖）、血氧量測、非侵入式血糖監測等多種生醫感測技術，並介紹穿戴式裝置、智慧醫療與腦機介面（BCI）等新興應用。

課程採分組實驗與專題實作相結合的方式，學生將從基本儀器與量測原理出發，學習生醫電子系統的設計、實作與資料分析，並進行創新應用的期末專題開發。透過課程訓練，學生不僅能建立生醫訊號量測與分析的專業基礎，亦能培養團隊協作、問題解決與跨領域創新之能力。
課程目標:
培養生醫電資工程與科學領域之專業人才，推動新興醫療與健康科技應用。

訓練學生熟悉生醫電子量測工具與方法，具備跨領域實作能力。

鞏固學生在硬體、軟體與資料分析上的綜合技能。

培養獨立研究與創新思考能力，能發掘、分析並解決生醫工程相關問題。
課程要求:
本課程分為兩個階段：

階段一：生醫量測基礎與工具操作

實驗一：基本生醫信號量測 (EEG, ECG, EMG 等)

實驗二：生醫信號量測電路之分析與設計

實驗三：穿戴式裝置生醫量測實驗 (以智慧手錶 ECG 為例)

階段二：期末專題實作

以腦機介面（BCI）為主題，針對指定應用題目分組進行設計與驗證

包含資料收集、系統開發、成果展示與效能評比

課程概述:
固態物理學是學習電子元件及光電元件的基本科目之ㄧ。本課程將從晶體結構出發，讓同學了解固態材料尤其是半導體晶體材料的基本結構特性以及電子能帶特性。授課大綱基本上依照教科書的編排，可分列如下： 
1. Crystal structure
2. Wave diffraction and the reciprocal lattice
3. Crystal binding and elastic constants
4. Phonons: crystal vibration
5. Phonons: thermal properties
6. Free electron Fermi gas
7. Energy bands

本課程將以Kittel固態物理教本為主要內容教學。

在課程中會用到普通物理、化學、近代物理與工程數學。用到時請複習相關的章節與內容。第二章 reciprocal lattice 用到 Fourier transform 請特別複習工程數學。reciprocal lattice 是XRD, TEM 等重要量測技術 以及 electronic band structure 的基礎。
第三章 後半部是 elastic constants 會用到張量以及剪力請先複習工程數學，這個部分將可幫助我們分析計算半導體或其他材料內部的strain。

9. Transfer Learning

課程概述:
工業控制系統廣泛運用於軌道與道路運輸、能源、煉油、水處理、海上航行、智慧製造，甚至應用於智慧建築、智慧家庭、智慧城市等未來數位生活，工業控制系統聯網後，成為駭客攻擊新目標，所造成之危害與損失比傳統企業更為嚴重。工業控制系統注重保證安全(Safety)，其資安防護要求異於傳統企業資安防護方法，資安(Security)若未做好，則工業安全沒辦法被保證，如何做好Security for Safety(S4S)是當前控制系統資安首重議題。
數位元素已深入生活各層面，其資訊安全問題已不只影響資料外洩與隱私問題，甚至影響人身安全、經濟損失與營運中斷問題，歐盟已因應這些韌性疑慮要求所有出口到歐盟具數位元素之產品，要求都要通過資安韌性法案要求才給予CE標章，才可上市。此外AI在工業應用中的重要性也在迅速增長，企業幾乎無法拒絕使用AI，例如語言助手和聊天機器人、腫瘤診斷圖像識別系統、與工廠人員互動的工業機器人或自動駕駛汽車。國際對於AI應用在AIoT(人工智慧物聯網)/IIoT(工業物聯網)，甚至醫療、車輛移動等智慧應用的安全及可信賴之要求已開始制定標準，對於AI應用，AI基礎主題需要與橫向主題相結合，以及相關的經濟和應用領域(如工控、醫療、自駕等)，鑑於應用程序的多樣性、複雜性和動態性，國際認為AI有必要基於風險的評估才能進行應用，未來AI應用的要求將重視Safety與Security，將根據其使用案例、道德和風險程度來與各種領域應用相結合。
本課程授課著重專業知識與實作技術訓練並重，專業知識上首先介紹各領域AI應用、工控應用與工控系統基礎概念、剖析AI、工控與IoT攻擊手法、介紹可信任AI的標準和規範、介紹工控系統設備與網路結構、簡介工控資安防護技術方案、講授國際對於工業系統的資安標準要求與防護工程實施做法，在實作技術訓練方面依據每次課程熟悉工控系統資安防護漸進概念程度，同步以模擬工控網路進行工控資安防護技術實作訓練，包括簡易工控網路行為分析與攻防技術練習，並引導學生完成一份主機網路行為語威脅分析報告，期末以實機上線演練測試學員工控資安分析與防護實務能力，以作為未來工業OT資安技術能力證明參考。課程最末亦針對歐盟網路韌性法案(CRA)及AI Safety與Security的相關內容進行介紹。
課程目標:
‧	  學習工控系統應用領域與網路架構
‧	  認識工控威脅攻擊手法
‧	  了解工控系統運作概念
‧	  熟悉工控網路封包分析操作
‧	  練習工控系統攻擊與防禦之網路分析操作
‧	  認識國際工控資安要求與做法(IEC 62443)
‧	  建立工控資安專業知識與防護技術能力技巧
‧	  掌握國際對AI應用安全要求趨勢
          介紹各類產業應用國際安全要求趨勢(含歐盟網路韌性法案CRA)發展
課程要求:

‧	對Matlab或C或一般程式語言有撰寫能力

課程概述: 本課程以 16 週時間，系統性探討生成式 AI 與創業的交互影響，並以「創業思維為主、技術實作為輔」為核心設計理念。課程前半段將引導學生建立創業思維，從人類需求出發，進行市場洞察、商業模式設計與市場推進策略的思考。後半段則聚焦於生成式 AI 技術的應用與實作，涵蓋 GPT-4 與 Gemini 等前沿工具，並透過案例分析與設計思考工作坊，協助學生將創業構想落實為具體的 AI 產品或服務。
課程目標:
1. 創業思維養成：協助學生掌握從人類需求出發到市場進入的完整創業邏輯。
2. 技術實踐能力：培養學生運用生成式 AI 技術進行系統開發與應用落地的能力。
3. 跨域整合：促進技術、商業與人文的跨領域思維，並推動長線創業生態的建立。
4. 倫理與風險意識：引導學生思考生成式 AI 帶來的倫理挑戰、法律規範與風險管理策略。
5. 專案驗證與實務對接：透過團隊專題與 Demo Day，完成從創業構想到市場驗證的實務流程。

開課系所: 生態學與演化生物學研究所 / 生物多樣性學分學程
課程概述:
人口爆炸、氣候變遷、非永續的經濟發展等人為因素，對地球生態造成前所未有的巨大壓力。生物多樣性正急速降低，物種滅絕速率遽增百倍以上；許多物種在生物學家還未有機會認識之前，就已遭遇滅絕的命運。生態系統各個組成分子環環相扣，失序的自然將直接威脅人類的健康和經濟，因此搶救地球生態刻不容緩！

    面對人類未來發展前所未有的多元挑戰，我們必須在傳統的高等教育課程中另闢蹊徑，整合跨領域的知識、教育及研究，讓學生除了知識的提升外，有機會接觸更多元的資源，從博物館、動植物園、種源庫、課堂及田野實習，瞭解地球生物的多樣性、物種間的互動、動植物的照護、環境議題的多面向，培養紮實的研究能力基礎。

    然而，擁有生物多樣性的博學知識亦將仍無法面對地球的快速變化，透過跨領域及與多方權益關係方建立夥伴關係，共同討論、設計，以促進研究、動員網絡、激發創新等方式，將知識轉化為行動才真的有可能將世界轉變為可持續發展的樣貌。為此，全球科學界因而起動”未來地球Future Earth”之科學平台，藉由全球數十個與永續發展相關的研究項目，綜合考慮地球的所有部分，尤其包括人類社會如何與地球系統相互連接與影響彼此，該平台並定義了所謂的”人類世(Anthropocene)”，即為人類對地球所留下的痕跡而建構出地球地質歷史的新紀元，Future Earth執行董事Amy Luers更以下列說明闡述了這個時代所需要的跨領域作法，以克服氣候與環境變遷帶來的種種挑戰 :

“We urgently need a radical shift in how global society interacts with Earth. Human activities today are disrupting our planet in ways that threaten our air quality, water reliability, food security, and the stability of our climate and ecosystems. Real transformations to overcome these challenges will only happen if we work together – science, technology, business, government, and civil society – as one.”
    

【系列課程規劃】
此課程乃為期一年的系列課程：
(1)	「永續未來與生態學I」－
第一學期將以介紹何謂「未來地球Future Earth」與「永續Sustainability」開始，建立學生未來地球、永續未來的整體概念及“相關科學議題的現況與發展；接著介紹各類生物在地球上的起源、演化歷史、相關生態學概念與科研課題、保育現況和未來展望、氣候變遷衝擊的課程內容，以建立學生對各類生物與相關生態學的基礎概念。隨後，導入人文社會、經濟、環境、健康、災害、水資源規劃等面向的內容，及早帶領學生發展跨領域思考，此外，藉由任課教師邀請校內外專家學者面對面分享，說明其實際的執行方法、保育與推廣工作經驗及案例分享等；

(2)	「永續未來與生態學II」－
第二學期起始主軸為各大生態系統之介紹，並邀請地球科學及大氣科學領域專家開講，確實提供學生多領域的多元學習，此學期將延續上學期之面向，並著重於系統性思考(system thinking)與整合(integration)，使學生更為全面理解、體悟知識與行動之結合。同時，在此階段將培育學生規劃專題研究、資料分析、視覺化統計及文字溝通之能力，各學生亦將須選擇有興趣之實驗室，自主尋找專家學者指導，在學期中便開始執行較為長期(至少半年)之專題研究計畫；

(3)	「永續未來與生態學III」－
第三學期在暑期進行，學生必須參與至少一週的密集田野課程，培育學生實作能力；同時，亦須積極進行其專題研究，於學期末數校聯合成果發表會時完成口頭及書面報告。

   本系列課程將由國立清華大學生命科學院與生物資源保種研究中心製作線上統一課程，以單元方式呈現部分「I」與「II」課程內容，強調修課學生之自主學習。
課程目標:
結合線上課程、實際討論及田野實習等課程，培育有意獻身自然保育、地球永續研究與實務的青年學子自主學習成長、獨立思考之能力。

課程概述:
The development of theory plays an important role in advancing ecology as a scientific field. This three-unit course is for students at the graduate or advanced undergraduate level. The course will cover classic theoretical topics in ecology, starting from single-species dynamics and gradually build up to multispecies models. The course will primarily focus on population and community ecology, but we will also briefly discuss models in epidemiology and ecosystem ecology. Emphasis will be on theoretical concepts and corresponding mathematical approaches.

This course is designed as a two-hour lecture (written on black/white board) followed by a one-hour hands-on practice module. In the lecture, we will analyze dynamical models and discuss their theoretical implications.. In the hands-on practice section, we will use a combination of analytical problem sets, interactive applications, and numerical simulations to gain a general understanding of the dynamics and behavior of different models.
課程目標: By the end of the course, students are expected to be familiar with the basic building blocks of ecological models and would be able to formulate and analyze simple models of their own. The hands-on practice component should allow students to link their ecological intuition with the underlying mathematical model, helping them to better understand the primary literature of theoretical ecology.
課程要求: Students are only expected to have a basic understanding of calculus (e.g., freshman introductory course) and Ecology. It's OK if you're not familiar with calculus as we will provide relevant material for you to review during the first week. The final grade consists of: assignment problem sets (60%), midterm exam (15%), final exam (15%), and participation (10%).

課名: 典藏自然：自然史博物館巡禮

課程概述:
自然史博物館是典藏、保存並詮釋自然世界的重要機構，收藏範圍從化石、植物到動物，乃至與自然相關的文化物件。它們在科學研究、教育推廣以及社會公共參與中，扮演不可或缺的角色，同時既是生物多樣性的檔案庫，也是文化交流的平台。
本課程將介紹自然史博物館的基礎與當代角色。我們將討論探索與蒐藏如何奠定博物館的基礎，典藏如何保存與管理，博物館如何與社會溝通，以及如何回應數位典藏與倫理爭議等新挑戰。課程不僅是概念性的學習，學生也將實際參與其中：透過作業，練習館藏解說與展覽企劃評估；並在期末以小組合作的方式，策劃並公開展示一個小型展覽。
課程目標:
修習本課程後，學生應能：
1.	理解自然史博物館在歷史與當代的角色。
2.	認識典藏保存、編目與其在研究與教育上的應用方式。
3.	批判性地思考與典藏、展覽相關的倫理與社會議題。
4.	練習簡要表達與自然史館藏解說的能力。
5.	評估並提供建設性的展覽企劃回饋。
6.	運用課程所學，規劃並完成小組策展，面向公眾展示。

This course includes two assignments and one final project. Detailed guidelines will be provided separately.
1.	Assignment 1 (Week 4)
o	Individual lightning talk introducing a natural history object.
o	Purpose: practice concise presentation and explore museum resources.
o	個人閃電報告，介紹一件自然史館藏。
o	目的：訓練簡要的口頭表達，並探索博物館資源。
2.	Assignment 2 (Weeks 9–12)
o	Group exhibition proposal with peer review and progress check.

o	目的：鼓勵提早準備，培養批判性評估與反覆修正的能力。
3.	Final Project (Weeks 14–16)

課名: 給每個人的演化生物學
開課系所: 無授課對象 / 生物多樣性學分學程
課程概述: 演化學與遺傳學是生物學的根基,我們所看到繽紛的世界都是生物在面臨生存競爭中，透過遺傳變異代代累積所展現出的適應結果。本課程將以人類的演化歷程為主，並分成三大部分。第一部分(1-4)介紹演化與遺傳學的基本概念，包含基礎遺傳學(2)、突變、基因漂變(3)與天擇(4)。第二部分(5-10)從這些基本概念出發解釋我們所看到的生命現象，包含複製子的概念(5)、合作行為如何演化(6)、適應的代價(7)、老化的現象(8)、為何會有癌症(9)、以及物種的特化(以人類為例,10)。第三部分追溯現代人類的起源(11-13)，討論不同族群的適應(11)、人類的遷徙(12)、原住民與南島語族的起源(13)。
課程目標: 本課程主要目標是讓非生物相關科系的學生瞭解遺傳學與演化學的基本原理。學生在掌握這些原理之後,能夠理解生命在如何掙扎中求生,並且形塑我們看到的生命世界的多樣性。

The primary functions of natural history museums include the collection, research, and exhibition of objects such as animal, plant, and microbial specimens, as well as mineral and fossil samples. This course provides students with practical learning opportunities in natural history museums, aiming to cultivate talents in museum education, research, collections management, exhibitions, and cultural and creative marketing.
The course’s practical training is centered on natural history-related museums within NTU, including the NTU Herbarium (Session 01), Museum of Zoology (Session 02), and NTU Insect Museum (Session 03). Students from all sessions will have a joint class in the first week and select two of the rotation museums. Students will rotate through internships at these two museums, each for two weeks, from Weeks 2-5. In the sixth week, students will need to present a proposal for a specific internship project in the selected museum for the second half of the semester, it could be individual project or a group project. By the end of the semester, students must deliver an oral presentation based on their internship report.
課程要求:
本課程的設計為博物館實習，且為領域專長「自然史與博物館」之總整課程，故建議學生預先修習「生物多樣性概論/生物多樣性的人文思維」、「演化生物學」、「典藏自然」、「生物科學繪圖」或類似課程，至少修畢三門，或同學期正在修習。實習中並需在課堂上進行一次進度報告。實習結束前，學生應準備書面實習報告，並在期末以口頭方式進行簡報。
The design of this course is on-site exercise in the museum. This course is also the cap-stone course of the specialization program ‘Natural history study and museums’, therefore, taking the following courses (or equivalent) in advantage is encouraged: ‘Introduction to Biodiversity / Science Communication and Biodiversity’, ‘Evolutionary Biology’, ‘Archiving Nature’, and ‘Biological Scientific Illustration’. Students must have taken at least three of the courses above, or taking it/them in current semester. There will be progress reviews during the semester, and the students need to prepare a written report before the end of internship. An oral presentation is required at the end of the semester.

開課系所: 電機工程學研究所 / 元件材料與異質整合博士學位學程 / 元件材料與異質整合碩士學位學程 / 生醫電子與資訊學研究所 / 電子工程學研究所

This course is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the cutting-edge processes and technologies pivotal to the semiconductor and display industries. Participants will gain in-depth knowledge of the front-end, middle-end, and back-end processes involved in the manufacturing of logic and memory semiconductors, including essential packaging techniques.
The curriculum will also offer a detailed exploration of the Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) and Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) processes critical to the production of Liquid Crystal Displays (LCDs). Furthermore, the course will cover the advanced encapsulation processes for Organic Light Emitting Diodes (OLED) and Micro-LEDs, highlighting the latest innovations in display technology.
Instruction will be delivered by a distinguished team of experts, all of whom hold Ph.D. degrees or possess over two decades of extensive experience in the semiconductor and display sectors, holding senior positions such as Technical Director, Senior Product Manager, and Product Director. A special lecture will be delivered by Erix Yu, Group Vice President of AMAT and President of AMT. Upon successful completion of the course, attendees will be awarded a certificate from AMT, recognizing their enhanced expertise in these advanced technological fields.

課程目標:
根據首先具體提出「創業精神」概念的經濟學家熊彼德(Joseph Alois Schumpeter,
1883~1950)所述，創業者重新組合產品、技術、市場、資源與組織等面向裡既有元
素，敢於改寫市場中的遊戲規則，且能在「不斷變動崩解的土地上」站穩腳跟。創業
者因此打破市場中或者有之的均衡狀況，讓「動態失衡」不斷發生，成為經濟發展的
主要動能。
在這樣的意義下，本課程以一學期的時間，針對背景各殊而都懷抱創業心志的EiMBA
同學，透過概念架構講授、個案討論、聚焦實作、新興模式觀摩、業間實務經驗分享
等方式，系統性探討創業者面對當代市場與顧客時宜有的理解。課程將由討論行銷的
本質開始，透過對於洞察消費者行為的深入分析與數位時代的價值創造、遞送、溝通
脈絡，探究當代創業者應掌握的行銷策略與戰術，
由於市場發展與產業演進的特殊路徑，台灣各業一方面對於行銷的理解較為浮面，另
一方面也較晚認知到創業的重要。透過多維度的探討，本課程希望透過消費者理論深
度探索與行動學習教學設計，幫助修課同學見樹且見林，思考數位時代各種創業可能
下的行銷邏輯，並透過環繞著顧客與市場的踏實理解，對進行中或未來的創業實務有
所助益。

開課系所: 創業創新管理碩士在職專班
課程概述:
「財務報導」（Financial Reporting, 以下簡稱 FR）在結構上分為外部財務報導與內部成 本管理會計等兩個模組。外部財務報導模組旨於介紹財務會計之基本概念與分析、運用，藉 以引導 EIMBA 學生瞭解財務資訊在資本市場之角色，進而能夠以財務資訊使用者的觀點，認 識財務會計與經濟決策之間的關係。本模組搭配「壽司幹嘛轉來轉去？！：你一定用得到 的財務知識」的章節，介紹學習會計如何幫助公司經營管理，以引導學生運用財務資訊作成 有用之經濟決策。本課程也結合實務會計師以及五家新創公司的分享。 

第二個模組是有關成本管理會計，運用成本資訊於內部營運決策是成功經理人的必備技能， 透過瞭解成本系統的運作方能以更合理的成本資訊來提昇企業競爭力。本模組目的在引導 EIMBA 學生瞭解基本成本管理議題，包括產品成本的計算、成本習性、作業基礎成本法及獲 利分析等議題。
課程目標: 在學習的態度上，本課程期望學習者能從資金提供者的角度，從公司財務報導去發掘企業的 競爭環境，企業的營運模式，企業的競爭優勢。在學習方法上，本課程強調學習者須要透過 練習增加自己對數字的敏感度，並參與討論與個案學習，並輔以課前閱讀的教材資料。本課 程的最終目的希望企業知道如何透過財務報導把公司的核心競爭優勢傳達給股東，同時資金 提供者如何從財務報導中發現企業的經營風險。

課程概述: 「策略管理」（Strategic Management）旨在探討企業整體與個別事業單位所面臨的策略性決策（strategic decisions），以及其思考與分析邏輯。不同於作業性的決策，策略性決策係所有決策的源頭、關乎組織的長期發展方向、並牽涉各功能領域的整體考量，因此，必須以多元、整體與永續的角度進行決策分析。因此在MBA的課程傳統上，策略管理常被安排在碩士班二年級畢業之前修習，被稱為是capstone course。
課程目標:

在學習方法上，本課程強調學習者的參與討論與透過個案的學習。本課程的最終目的在建構學習者明確的策略思考架構與策略分析方法，從而強化經營者的策略管理能力。

This course will meet weekly in a formal seminar format. Each week, a leading scientist will present his or her ongoing research (approximately 50 min, but can be longer). After each presentation, a Q&A session will be held.

Students take this course on a pass/fail basis. This course has no exams, and thus the grade is solely determined by the attendance. Two or more absences will result in an F (fail). Students who must miss a seminar may consult with the course instructor prior to the absence, but it is unlikely that an absence is excused. A tardiness of 10 min or more is treated as an absence.

In addition to the attendance, students are required to submit a report immediately after each seminar. Forms are distributed prior to a seminar. Students must write the evaluation/critique of a seminar. A report that is too rough/vague (including blank report) should not be submitted.

- To experience how scientific information is transmitted (the 50-min presentation style is one of the main modes of scientific presentation)

- To develop an own idea about what a good seminar is

Course Description 
農藥為高考必考科目,農藥也是植物保護(昆蟲,植病)相關類科主要的產業,而本課程涵蓋農藥學最重要之殺蟲劑部分,課程主軸將會著重於殺蟲劑分類、作用機制探討及與環境之關係。本課程對於參加高考或將來進入業界或生計產業均是必備基礎知識，課程可分三大部份
一、毒理學之基本原理—包括毒物動力學(Toxicodynamics)、計算毒理學(computional toxicology)
二、殺蟲劑之分類、作用標的、與作用機制
三、殺蟲劑之應用、管理、抗藥性及造成之環境議題
Course Objectives
1.	瞭解各種殺蟲劑應用於害蟲防治現況。 
2.	瞭解殺蟲劑之發展背景及應用於害蟲防治歷史。 
3.	認識各種殺蟲劑種類及化學特性。 
4.	瞭解殺蟲劑於害蟲體內之動態變化(toxicodynamics)。
5.	瞭解各種殺蟲劑之作用機制、選擇性。 
6.	瞭解殺蟲劑之使用限制及對環境之影響。
7.	瞭解殺蟲劑之風險評估及法規管理 。
8.	瞭解不同殺蟲劑之交相作用及影響 。
9.	瞭解害蟲抗藥性之發生與對策。 
Textbook
1.	Insecticide mode of action, edited by Joel R. Coats, Academic press
2.	Insecticide action : from molecule to organism, edited by Toshio Narahashi and Janice E. Chambers, New York : Plenum Press
3.	Toxicology of insecticide,  edited by Fumio Matsumura, New York : Plenum Press

課程概述: A three-credit introductory to microbiology course for environmental engineers comprised of two main sections: (1) classroom lectures, includes: the fundamentals of microbiology and the application of these fundamental microbial principles to environmental systems; and (2) laboratory sessions which students can learn basic microbial techniques. For lab sessions, students will practice several methods such as water sampling, membrane filtration, isolation, purifications, PCR and DNA sequencing. The goals of the course are to provide a solid foundation in microbial principles to complement courses addressing biological processes in environmental systems, and to provide a framework for research in microbial systems.
課程目標:
1. Explore how microorganisms drive biogeochemical cycles (e.g., nitrogen, sulfur, carbon) and their relevance to engineered and natural systems.
2. Learn the structural, metabolic, and ecological diversity of microorganisms, including bacteria, archaea, fungi, viruses, and protozoa, especially those relevant to water, soil, and waste environments.
3. Gain proficiency in classical and modern techniques used to study environmental microbes.
4. Understand the role of microbes in water/wastewater treatment, resource recovery (e.g., anaerobic digestion, bioleaching), bioremediation, and pathogen control.
5. Evaluate the occurrence, survival, and control of microbial pathogens and antibiotic-resistant bacteria in water, air, and soil. Understand monitoring and risk assessment frameworks.
課程要求: This course includes both lecture and laboratory sessions to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of environmental microbiology. Each week, students are required to attend a 2-hour lecture covering fundamental concepts and current research topics, as well as a 3-hour laboratory session focused on hands-on experience with microbial techniques relevant to environmental engineering. Students will complete one group laboratory report for the lab sessions to demonstrate data analysis, scientific writing, and teamwork skills. The course also includes midterm and final exams, assessing students' conceptual understanding and ability to apply microbiological principles to real-world environmental challenges.

A preliminary course on mathematical programming and decision analysis. 
Format:

課程目標:
Environment is a complex system. Different environmental problems are interrelated. To make a decision on how to solve environmental problem will inevitable face complexity and uncertainty. Environmental systems analysis is an approach to making decisions on solving environmental problems. It is based on systems thinking, i.e., considering the environment using the concept of systems. A system is an assembly of elements related in an organized whole. The components and the relations between the components in a system and their changes in time are the subjects to be investigated. The course includes three parts: mathematical programming, systems dynamics, and decision analysis. Mathematical programming is an optimization technique that searches for an optimal solution using a mathematical model. Systems dynamics is a tool for delineating the relations between the components in a system. Decision analysis is a formal way of constructing a decision under uncertainty. In addition, the students are divided into groups to perform case studies so that the students can learn how to use the systems analysis methods to analyze an environmental problem and obtain solutions. 

The goals of this course are to provide students with: 1. Mathematical programming; 2. The tools of systems analysis; 3. Software practice experience; and 4. Application in solving complex problems. The format of the course needs“discuss, conduct, and present” preliminary analysis. Discussion and interaction are emphasized.

課名: 環境與職業流行病學之暴露評估計量模擬及應用
開課系所: 公共衛生學系 / 環境與職業健康科學研究所
課程概述:
空氣汙染的量測誤差會影響相關健康效應的評估，而誤差的來源包括暴露濃度在時序上的變異以及量測的計量方式。本課程將透過Excel試算表，針對可逆(reversible)、不可逆(irreversible)、等比例(proportional)及超過閾值而誘發(discrete)之四類健康效應，進行汙染物暴露濃度模擬，以了解暴露計量(exposure metrics) 包含之變異性，並探討暴露計量與體內劑量之關係，以及可能之誤差。建此基礎之上，本課程將引導學生應用上述模擬之結果及觀察，針對課程指定之文獻進行回顧及批判分析，提出該文獻暴露評估之限制，進一步於期末報告利用分組方式，結合暴露計量觀念提出可行之研究設計及解決方案。

Hazardous exposures are usually complex with extended temporal processes leading to the development of biological responses, “damage/adverse responses/health effects”. A study intended to determine the quantitative relationship between exposure and risk of the effect requires a careful matching of the temporal variation in exposure with the kinetics of uptake, distribution and metabolism and matching those to the dynamics of response. However, bias and attenuation of the health risk estimate can be introduced when there is exposure error in air pollution measurement. Adequate exposure metrics may provide a means of reducing error (leading to less bias and uncertainty in health risk estimates) if they capture variability in exposure, which depends on the study design, health outcome, and pollutant of interest.

To enable this, the course will start from a review of the basic components of exposure assessment for air pollution and subsequently introduce exposure metrics for four types of health outcomes: different combination of reversible/irreversible and discrete/proportional outcomes. Students will develop knowledge of exposure determinants and its temporal behavior (variability), in conjunction with skills for modeling temporal behavior of exposures and outcomes through simulations using excel spreadsheets . Guided critical analysis of publications will be performed, and information from simulations will be used to design an exposure assessment matched to the biology of the adverse effect(s) . In the finals, the class will culminate with a design project where small groups of students design a new study of a specific exposure and hypothesized effect(s) reported in a previously critiqued scientific paper. 


評分說明 Grading : 

1.	期中考 – 本課程透過期中考來評估學生對於課程基礎概念之理解程度。考題包含(但不限於)簡短申論題以及個案討論與分析。學生應具備以下幾個面向之基礎知識和分析技能：(1)了解流行病學之暴露評估中的專有名詞和概念的定義；(2) 指出適合個案研究中探討疾病之相對應的暴露計量模型；(3)描述個案研究中所使用來評估暴露與疾病關係之方法。

2.	課堂參與 - 學生分組後，依據課堂練習（測驗和個案研究）之題目進行小組討論。過程中，學生了可以藉此機會釐清不懂的觀念並與同儕分享、說明重要觀念，同時也能透過邏輯思考以找出題目中的重要問題及討論面向。

課程概述: 本課程內容包括各國職業安全衛生立法歷史及民法、刑法、行政法與勞動立法之關係，國際職業安全衛生政策、立法與推動策略；我國職業安全衛生法、勞動檢查法之立法理念，水平及垂直立法之架構，並針對物理、化學、生物、人因危害與社會影響勞工心理健康潛在威脅因子之辨識、分析、評估、控制與職業健康服務實務探討我國職業安全衛生法、勞動檢查法重要預防規章及其相關制度之發展。另就社會保險職業災害預防、通報、診斷、認定、補償、重建之國際立法趨勢及職傷病診斷實務，探討我國甫於2022年勞動節實施之勞工職業災害保險及保護法，使學生對國際職業安全衛生與職業災害勞工保護之立法有宏觀及深入瞭解，並提出心得報告。

課名: 傳染病防治: 倫理與法律實務
開課系所: 傳染病學學程 / 公共衛生學系 / 健康政策與社會研究學分學程 / 法律學系 / 法律研究所 / 流行病學與預防醫學研究所
課程概述:
傳染病有其特殊性。傳染性疾病與非傳染性疾病最大的差別在於，傳染病會透過人與人或者環境來達到擴散的目的，導致生命財產的損失。從流感大流行、SARS疫情的慘痛經驗、多重抗藥性結核病的氾濫、愛滋病人及其他性傳染病的被標籤化、伊波拉病毒肆虐西非導致貧民區宵禁等，我們又學到什麼? 
在傳染病的防治與控制的思考上，個人的權利和群體的利益，不時會有相互衝撞的問題。法律是最低的生活標準，也是社會運作的底線，當有發生群突發的可能時，除了依法行政以外，是否也要考慮，回歸到倫理這個社會賴以運作的常規來處理呢? 
本課程將由授課教師本身的傳染病防治實務經驗講授與介紹，給予同學傳染病防治及公共衛生單位，在工作推動過程中真實面臨的倫理困境；搭配特定疾病，就實務和理論，進行深入的批判和討論，讓同學能夠在課程中，增加自我批判省思的能力，以期於課程後，對相關議題有獨立判斷面對挑戰的能力。

Communicable disease is quite different from non-communicable disease. Communicable disease can spread due to direct human to human contact or human to human contact mediated by the environment. In either case, communicable disease can lead to great losses of both life and property. But what have we learned from outbreaks of communicable disease? From influenza pandemics, lessons from Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS), emergency of multi-drug resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB), the stigmatization of sexually-transmitted diseases such as acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS) to curfews in Western Africa meant to curb the spread of Ebola in Monrovia's West Point slum; there have been many lessons, but what have we actually learned?
The Communicable Disease Act gives the government the power to intervene--when necessary--in the private sector for the preservation of the health, safety, and morals of the community. Pursuant to this constitutional authority, all counties and cities have enacted public health statutes designed to control the spread of communicable diseases by using measures such as civil commitment, which infringe upon civil rights. Statutes, though, are fundamentally limited; they represent nothing more than the letter of the law, whereas ethics and morality represent the spirit of laws. So in regards to these public health statues, how can we adopt appropriate ethical considerations when implementing the Communicable Disease Act to preserve integrity?
The course will be led by an instructor (teacher) with extensive knowledge of communicable diseases and field experience in the control of communicable diseases. The instructor will provide examples of ethical predicaments that frontline public health workers will be forced to face. Field experiences and concepts will be discussed and criticized in relation to specific communicable diseases. Students participating in the course will learn how to think critically and develop the ability to face challenges and to find solutions to problems in the field independently.
課程目標:
本課程是希望透過對傳染病防治及公共衛生實務工作所發生之相關問題介紹，啟發同學對傳染病在倫理和法律相關議題的興趣。此外亦希望透過本課程使同學了解預防醫學相關措施及研究之人權維護及倫理議題，包括:
(1)	現行傳染病相關防治法規內容為何，包括在個案、接觸者及其暴露之空間的規範；
(2)	傳染病防治採用強制隔離的目的及手段、與實務執行層面所面臨的程序正義；
(3)	現行防治規範、措施可能存在的問題和改善的空間。

The aim of this course is to stimulate an interest in ethics and legal issues associated with communicable disease control and public health field work. Students who'd like to participate in the course will learn to understand human right and ethical issues related to preventive strategies and research including: 
(1)	The content of the current version of the Communicable Disease Act, including the statues related to cases, contacts and exposed environments.
(2)	The goals and strategies for compulsory isolation to impede the spread of diseases, and the requirements, safeguards, and due process related to civil commitment.
(3)	Demonstration of the limitations of and possible problems with current statutes and other major deficiencies in public health law.

This course is designed to establish foundational competencies in epidemiology for students, with an emphasis on mastering causal inference, data analysis, and critical thinking. The curriculum is organized into three sections:
1. Study Design: This module covers the principles of causal inference and the elements
involved in designing epidemiological studies.
2. Analytical Methods: This section introduces the principles of data analysis, including the practical application of statistical methods for analyzing epidemiological data.
3. Critical Appraisal: This segment develops students' skills in independently evaluating the credibility of scientific papers, fostering critical thinking.

Textbooks and Materials:
- Primary Textbook: Rothman KJ, Epidemiology: An Introduction. New York: Oxford University Press, 2012.
- Supplementary readings and resources will be provided for specific topics throughout the course.

1. Master the principles of causal inference to critically evaluate scientific literature and conduct rigorous research for their master's thesis.
2. Acquire a thorough understanding of how to design various types of epidemiological studies, including clinical trials, descriptive studies, cohort studies, and case-control studies
3. Learn to recognize the effects of random variation and bias in research findings and apply statistical methods to effectively analyze epidemiological data
4. Gain the capability to critically assess the validity and applicability of empirical research findings

課名: 生物醫學統計專題討論D1
開課系所: 流預所生物醫學統計組
課程概述:
由每一位修課學生需針對特定主題選取一篇原著生物統計/健康數據拓析方法或理論型論文進行口頭報告並回答問題，其他同學則需評論與提問。 
In the course, each student is required to select an original methodology or application paper in biostatistics/health data analytics for their oral presentation. After presenting, they will respond to comments and questions from the audience. Students who are not presenting are also expected to actively participate by providing comments and asking questions on the presentations.
課程目標:
本課程藉由閱讀與討論生物統計/健康數據拓析之理論與方法相關文獻，將訓練學生成為相關專業人員，學習如何發掘及定義健康資料統計分析之研究議題，進而培養獨立解決問題的能力，增進科學表達以及學術專業寫作能力。

This course entails reading and engaging in discussions on original methodology or application papers of biostatistics and health data analytics. Through this training, we anticipate to equip the students with the ability to identify and formulate research questions, cultivate independent problem-solving skills, and enhance their scientific communication and academic writing capabilities as a biostatistician.
課程要求:
1.	論文選擇與上傳：
(1)	由每一位修課學生針對特定主題，選取一篇原著生物統計/健康數據拓析方法或理論型論文於安排時間進行口頭報告。 
(2)	所選論文必須於報告前4週寄給助教，方便助教上傳於NTU COOL上，以作為評論同學及修課同學聽取報告時之準備工作。 
1. Paper selection and upload
(1) Each student in the course is required to select an original methodology or application article in biostatistics/health data analytics for oral presentation.
(2) Presenters must send their selected papers to the course TA 4 weeks prior to the presentation (to be uploaded to NTUCOOL) such that other students can prepare their comments in advance.

2.	報告時間與方式： 
(1)	修課學生須以英文進行口頭報告。博士班學生每人報告之時間約為30~40分鐘，碩士班每人報告20分鐘，請斟酌投影片頁數。
(2)	在口頭報告最末必須提供1-2頁投影片，並口頭以英文表達整個報告總結。 
(3) 報告者需再當天9 am前將投影片上傳至NTUCOOL。
2. Presentation time and format
(1) Students are required to give the oral presentations in English. Presentations are limited to 30-40 minutes for doctoral students and 20 minutes for master's students. Please organize your slides accordingly.
(2) At the end of the presentation, the presenter must summarize the paper in 1-2 slides.
(3) Presenters must upload their presentation slides to NTUCOOL no later than 9 am on the day of the class.

3.	評論與討論： 
(1)	每次報告之後，有20~40分鐘討論時間，由3-4位事先指定的同學擔任評論員進行評論，報告同學則針對評論意見進行回應(鼓勵使用英文但非強制)。其他非指定評論同學也歡迎針對報告內容提問。
(2)	授課教師們會在報告最後輪流提問，並給予意見及反饋。 
3. Comments and discussions
(1) A 20-40 minute discussion will follow each presentation. 3-4 students will be assigned as commentators to give a review and ask questions on the presentation (English encouraged but not mandatory). Presenters must respond in detail based on their understanding of the method and principles of the paper. Other students are encouraged to join the discussion.
(2) At the end of the Q&A session, instructors will provide comments, suggestions, and an overall evaluation of the presentation.

4.	每週評論作業：
(1) 當周非報告者在課程後需繳交一份簡短的評論報告(中文/英文皆可)，並於當天11:59 pm前上傳至NTUCOOL。
(2) 報告者無需針對自己當週的內容撰寫報告，但仍須在其他周次繳交對他人報告的評論。
4. Weekly commenting assignments
(1) Students who are not assigned to present or comment should write a brief review of the presentations (in either English or Chinese) and upload it to NTUCOOL before 11:59 pm on the same day of the class.
(2) Presenters do not have to submit their own review but are still required to write a comment on other students' presentations.

本校尚無訂定 A+ 比例上限。

課程概述:
臺灣的農業與鄉村發展議題，不僅面臨青壯人力外移、人口老化的社會結構困境，農工產業競逐與轉型過程出現的衝突從未平息。面對自然環境與人口條件的變遷，並考量國家整體發展的需求，農村的價值亟需重新檢視，以促進資源的合理配置與人才培育，因應未來多重挑戰。隨著資通訊與能源科技的快速發展，農村在產業、生活與韌性面向上正迎來轉型契機。本課程聚焦臺灣與全球農業與鄉村的現況與問題、可行的解決方案、農鄉發展的創新方向，邀請不同領域的專家學者從實務、政策與理論觀點切入，增進同學對於農業與鄉村發展的認知與理解，協助同學發掘並培養對於生物產業傳播暨發展主要領域的學習興趣。
          114-1農鄉發展專題的課程內容與農委會農科院農政中心規劃之「當代農政議題論壇」結合，該論壇的目的在於提供關心農政、鄉村發展議題的倡議者、規劃者、行動者一個討論平台，透過跨域互動增進學術研究、實務工作及政策推動層面的交流與合作。2025年農政論壇關注當前農村與農業發展面對的挑戰與可能契機，規劃8場主題論壇以及1場綜合討論，期盼藉由實務工作者與學者專家之對話，深化修課同學與社會大眾對農鄉議題的關心與理解，進而凝聚共識並做為政策研擬的重要參考。

課名: 河川生態學：概念與應用
開課系所: 生物環境系統工程學系
課程概述: Fresh water is a fundamental constituent of life and is essential to a wide range of economic activities. In fact, fresh water also plays a key role in many biological and physical aspects of the ‘Earth system’. For example, water cycle is important in affecting the climatic changes and variability. Fresh water is a limited resource. Less than 0.01% of the world's water is easily accessible in lakes and rivers. However, global water use has increased 300% since 1950 and is growing faster than the Earth's population. The tragic effects of drought, flooding and water pollution have frequently seen in Taiwan and other parts of the world such as Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas as a consequent of over-use and mismanagement of water resources. Such problems are widespread and will be made more acute by accelerating demand on fresh water arising from trends in economic growth.
課程目標:
Course objectives:
–	Develop an understanding of physio-chemical and ecological aspects of the freshwater systems, especially for Taiwan rivers; 
–	Explain the causes and consequences of human modification of fresh waters, and their implications for conservation of aquatic biodiversity and maintenance of human well being;
–	Describe the techniques which may be used to quantify the status of (and monitor the changes in) instream and riparian ecological niches; and
–	Introduce the range of management strategies that can be used to reduce or mitigate human impacts on freshwater ecosystems and maintain water quality; in particular, the concept of drainage basin management. 

Course content 課程大綱:
–	Hydrology and physiography of flowing water, lakes and reservoirs, wetland habitats and groundwater 河川、湖泊、水庫、濕地及地下水生境之水文及環境特徵
–	Aquatic fauna, flora and microbes 水生動植物及微生物
–	Adaptations of freshwater organisms 水生生物對水環境之適應性
–	Periodic and stochastic events in fresh waters 淡水環境中的定期性與隨機性現象
–	River continuum concept 河川續動概念
–	Complex biological interactions 生物互相作用之關係
–	Synthesis: determinants of community structure 群聚結構之決定因素
–	Organic matter transformation and nutrient cycles 有機物質運輸及養分循環
–	Sampling stream and rivers 河川環境之採集技術
–	Human impacts in freshwater systems 人類對淡水系統影響
–	Monitoring and environmental impact assessment techniques in river systems 河川系統之監測及環境風險評估
–	Lake and reservoir management 湖泊及水庫之管理
–	Dam and flow regulation 水壩及河道整治
–	Conservation of freshwater biodiversity 淡水生物多樣性之保育

課程概述:
本課程介紹當代全球能源挑戰 - 如何在滿足日益增長的能源需求的同時，解決其造成的健康、環境和氣候方面的不利影響? - 的經濟學理論與相關的分析模擬方法。本課程側重於以永續方式滿足區域和全球能源需求，評估當前和潛在的未來能源系統，涵蓋各種可再生和傳統能源生產技術、能源最終使用種類和活動，以及影響能源需求、供應、價格和環境的各種公共政策。

This course presents the economics of the contemporary global energy challenge – how to satisfy growing energy demand while simultaneously addressing adverse health, environmental, and climate impacts. With an emphasis on meeting regional and global energy needs in a sustainable manner, this course assesses current and potential future energy systems, covering a variety of renewable and conventional energy production technologies, energy end-use practices and alternatives, and various public policies affecting energy demand, supply, prices, and environmental effects.
課程目標:

課程概述:
大學國文：文化思想與寫作（一）
本課程選讀先秦道家作品《莊子》，授課教材以教師自編講義發放為主。
春秋戰國時期為諸子百家爭鳴的時代，儒家的禮教文化、墨家的現實主義、道家的清靜無為及法家的嚴刑重法等，各學派均以各自所處的時代及所面臨的困境展開對一己生命的思索及對救世之道的探索，因而言論及主張往往有互相辯難之處。本課程以《莊子》內篇為綱，針對各篇中所提出之問題選讀其他學派中的相關篇章，分析其思想異同，期使學生能養成由不同角度看待問題的思維模式。
課程目標:
（1）通過各種代表性文本的精讀、解析及詮釋，加強學生的人文思維與涵養。
（2）訓練學生分析與思辨的基本能力，培養轉化知識或經驗的論述和表達能力。
（3）藉由實作與討論，充實文類知識，使學生逐步掌握寫作要點。
課程要求:
一、本課程進行方式為：
1. 先將文本讀過一次，大致理解字面意思，此階段不對文本之思想作深入的探討。
2. 老師就讀過之文本提出問題，由同學進行小組討論(腦力激盪)。
3. 在白板上簡要寫出小組討論結果後，推舉同學代表上台報告。
4. 總結

二、小組討論目標：
1. 一開始不先深入探討文本的思想，目的是希望同學能在不存在任何別人灌輸的先入為主的觀念前，從零開始，根據原文獨立思考。
2. 希望同學在小組討論時能發揮想像力，暢所欲言，無須介意意見之高低、好壞、對錯。
3. 藉由小組討論學習表達自我想法，同時聽取同學想法，吸收歸納為個人初步意見，並以簡潔的方式將之表達出來。
4. 由之後的各組發表意見中，得知小組之外成員的其他不同看法，進一步豐富對文本的理解。
5. 理解並尊重各種不同的理解及思維模式。

三、課程要求
1. 由於本課程將以小組討論方式進行，為了小組討論能順利進行，選修本課程之同學請勿無故缺席，有事無法到課者須事先至學生請假系統填寫假單。請假以三次為限。無故缺席或請假超過三次者每次扣平常分數10分。
2. 須繳交三篇作業，包括「文章競寫」一篇及作文兩篇，要求有個人見解並按時繳交作業。

A robot-proof model of higher education is not concerned solely with topping up students’ minds with high-octane facts. Rather, it refits their mental engines, calibrating them with a creative mindset and the mental elasticity to invent, discover, or otherwise produce something society deems valuable. This could be anything at all---a scientific proof, a hip-hop recording, a new workout regimen, a web comic, a cure for cancer. Instead of training laborers, a robot-proof education trains creators.

「創造」被視為二十一世紀的跨領域關鍵核心能力之一，甚至被視為人類有別於其他物種的獨特能力。人類「創造」的事物，可以是有形的或無形的、內容的或是實體的，從小說、圖畫、影音到學術論文，都屬於「創造」。雖然從人類創造事物開始就有相關的討論，然而「創造力」成為研究議題卻只有約莫百年的歷史。換句話說，當今我們談論的「創造力」並非恆久不變的，而是與現代科學研究及社會發展發展息息相關。

「給創作者的創造力」課程分為兩部分，一部分講授與討論創造力的「概念與議題」；另一部分則著重於「創作實踐」。在「概念與議題」中，我將介紹從關於「創造力」的不同定義以及理論模型，並帶領學生思考不同理論定義所帶來的社會、文化層面乃至實作上的意義為何。我們也將探索並討論創造力與未來社會發展的相關議題，從生成式AI到長壽時代的生命追尋，創造力的定義、意義乃至價值可能如何轉變，我們又該可能如何重新看到創造這件事。

在「創作實踐」中，我將介紹不同創作者所帶來的創作心法，並透過學生的親身演練與反思，加上同儕社群互助討論，探索生成式AI協作，培養出適用於自己的創作方法，讓「創造」不再限於靈光一閃的時刻，而是屬於創作者的創造之力。
課程目標:
1.    說出「創造力」做為一個概念的歷史發展與不同的定義。
2.    說出「創造力」的多元面向，及其與當代乃至未來社會與文化的關係。
3.    列出並實踐有助於「創造力」開展的方法。

學生修習本課程後將學會：
1.    逐步推進一個自主規劃的創作專案。
2.    應用理論相關的實踐方法，挹注於創作實踐的歷程。
3.    與他人討論階段性創作成果，並從中獲得對於創作實踐有助益的建議。
4.    使用生成式AI平台協作創作。

課程概述：
★本校有兩門課程介紹青少年的基本心理狀態：一為「發展心理學」、二為「青少年心理學」。發展心理學是一門以科學理論及方法了解個體在知覺、認知、語言、性格、情緒、人際關係等向度上之發展現象的學問，其所採取的是全人生（由出生到死亡）的觀點。青少年心理學則將現象的描述與理論的推演皆侷限於青少年階段。 但是，青少年此時此刻的行為並非憑空而來，難免與其天生氣質、發展藍圖、以及過去成長經驗有關。因此，本課程中會將發展心理學的基本理論與現有實徵研究結果做一簡介，再著重於對青少年期各發展主題之整合及其間關聯性的介紹。 

★這門課對修通識學分的學生來說，是體驗自我成長與深度關心社會的奠基石(corner stone)；對師培生來說，是學習分析與認識青少年心理的核心石(key stone)；對心理系高年級同學來說，是統整心理學知識的合頂石(cap stone)。 透過一面介紹發展心理學的理論及研究方法，一面按週以鷹架設計與每週批改發回的討論課會議記錄，本課程期望幫助同學以多元的全人角度，深入思考青少年面臨的成長衝擊。也透過心理學理論與方法的邏輯訓練，讓同學們練習以科學方法檢視自己對青少年及其成長環境如文化、家庭、師生、同儕、網路、道德、學習等議題的盲點。
課程目標:
課程目標：
★「青少年心理學」這門課，不會直接傳授班級經營或心理輔導的技巧。而是透過介紹心理學的理論及研究方法，幫助修習中等教育學程的同學在未來的職場上得以透過心理學的多元思維，深入思考青少年所面臨的成長衝擊。也透過心理學理論推演的邏輯訓練，讓同學們有一套方法來檢視自己在教學與班級經營上的盲點。 本課程一方面為師資培育中心之「增能課程」，另一方面為開放給全校之「通識課程」。這兩班合併上課，一方面召募到了關心青少年發展的未來師資，另一方面也廣納了本校具有不同學科領域專長的高年級和研究所同學。因為這樣的修課學生組合，使同學們在獲得基本的青少年心理學知識外，還透過小組討論與團體報告摩擦出了不同的溝通、領導、自省、關懷、及創新、超越的火花。 

★本課程的目標不止於介紹青少年心理學的理論、研究方法、及現象；並欲透過每週給予會議記錄回饋的小組討論鷹架系統，及期末「口頭報告嘉年華」與期末分組書面報告的批改，一方面幫助學生活化心理學的理論、方法與思考邏輯，另一方面也可從團隊協作中摩擦出對溝通、領導、協調、合作、公平分工、關懷、創新、及超越的火花與自省，因而也讓學生從自身修課經驗中體會在期初「組員招募市集」活動中便一再強調的：「青少年最需要的就是鼓勵、陪伴、歡笑、信任、以及歸屬感」。

課程概述:
Teaching Methods and Materials in English is a foundational course for those who are interested in English language teaching. It is a prerequisite course for Practicum in English and Internship in English, which together will help you prepare for your future language teaching career. 

The first half of the semester covers a review of methods and how to approach the idea of methods in more contextually-responsive ways. We will also be looking into the teaching of listening, speaking, reading, and writing – as well as vocabulary and grammar – with questions of context in mind. The second half of the semester is more “hands-on” in nature: we will examine some basic principles that are useful for designing a course, planning a lesson, and selecting / adapting / creating teaching materials. Throughout the semester we will discuss important debates in the field, and continuously reflect on the current landscape of English language teaching in Taiwan.
課程目標:
By the end of this course you will:
* Be familiar with the key developments and debates in the field.
* Know the basics of designing a course, planning a lesson, and selecting / adapting / creating relevant language teaching materials.
* Develop a preliminary set of language teaching principles that respond to various contextual and student needs.
* Start engaging in dialogues that deal with the tensions between theory and practice.

課程概述: 學生在修畢師資職前教育課程、通過教師資格考試後，始得修習本課程。學生運用與反思在專門課程、教育專業課程習得的知識及理論，進入與臺大簽約的教育實習機構進行為期半年的全時教育實習，內容包含：教學實習、導師（級務）實習、行政實習與研習活動，最後通過教育實習，取得教師證書。
課程目標: 本課程與公民與社會科的教材教法、教學實習兩門課程銜接，著重試教與熟稔課綱教材內容、班級經營、校園行政事務，以期為畢業後擔任教職工作奠定扎實基礎。
課程要求:
一、教學實習
（一）跟隨實習輔導老師入班，觀察與紀錄老師的教學策略與方法。
（二）掌握課綱與教材的核心概念、擬定教學流程、撰寫教案、製作教材。
（三）把握每次上台教學機會，並於教學前、後與實習輔導老師及指導老師討論。
（四）期末教學演示。

二、導師實習
（一）觀察實習輔導老師如何透過班會、週記、聯絡簿、社群媒體…等，建立導生的生活常規。
（二）觀察實習輔導老師如何在學校日如何與家長建立共識，並瞭解如何與家長溝通、聯繫，讓家長成為班級經營的助力。
（三）瞭解學校在學生輔導事務中的行政支援。
（四）透過實習輔導老師與學生資料表，瞭解學生的背景與學習狀況，習得問題防範的措施與如何處理長期與突發問題的方法。
（五）與導生相關的事務或訊息，務必注意保密與輔導倫理原則。

三、行政實習
（一）透過協助、參與各項行政工作，瞭解學校各行政單位的主要執掌、工作內容與運作。
（二）瞭解行政處室之間如何協調，以及行政人員與教師之間如何溝通、配合。

四、實習相關記錄文件、返校座談、研習活動
（一）準時繳交「全國教育實習資訊平臺」與「臺灣大學師資培育中心」規定文件與實習歷程檔案。
（二）積極參與每月的返校座談與研習、試教演練。
（三）參加校內、外舉辦相關的研習活動。

五、若有任何問題，請即時與指導老師聯繫，並共同尋求適當的解決方式，以期順利完成實習。

課程概述:
Principle of Communications is the first course to communication systems for undergraduate students, and it aims to uncover how a communication system works and the underlying beautiful theoretical principles. It builds the foundations for students to explore more advanced topics related to communications, ranging from theoretical development to practical implementation, such as wireless communications, wireless networks, Internet of Things, etc.. Lectures are developed to answer the following key question: how to reliably deliver information over an unreliable physical medium?  

Towards answering this question, we begin with the interface between the cyber and the physical world and explain how to convert from digital to analog and vice versa. Next, we introduce a first statistical model, the additive noise channel, that captures the unreliable feature of physical medium, and develop the principle for optimal reconstruction based on statistical decision theory. Then, we introduce the key concept of coding in order to achieve reliable communication, together with some concrete examples of codes. These principles are extended to further channel models, namely, wireline (telephone) channel and wireless channel, where additional challenges such as inter-symbol interference (ISI) and fading need to be tackled. OFDM is introduced to alleviate ISI while diversity techniques are developed to mitigate fading.
課程目標:
1) Introduce the basic principles of digital communication systems. 
2) Develop solid foundations to explore advanced topics related to communications, ranging from theoretical development to practical implementation. 
3) Build theory-oriented thinking and intuition in system design.

Optoelectronics include electronics and light. Generally, students in the Department of Electrical Engineering are unfamiliar with the light part, such as cameras, holograms, optical coatings, lasers, optical fiber communication, and other critical optoelectronic components. 
We will start with geometric optics for image formation, extending image quality examination to optical Fourier transform for image processing and hologram. Then we go into two-beam and multi-beam interferences, the former allows us to check optical quality and build up sensors while the latter leads to the foundation of optical coating and the basis of a laser. The course ends with the introduction of active and passive optical fiber optoelectronic components for contemporary topics such as transoceanic communications, biomedical sensing applications, and silicon photonics.
Because it is an introduction, the content of the course is easy to understand. There have been even freshman students from various departments who scored high marks. This course does not involve in- depth physics of semiconductors but will give highlights when needed.

Basic working principles of optoelectronics will be described and how they are applied and developed to become various devices such as LED, laser, photo-detector, solar cell, optical fibers, etc. in our daily life will be highlighted. The following topics are planned to be covered. 
1. Basic light properties and derived devices Ray, camera, and eye; Fourier transform in optics, diffraction, holography, and photo-lithography; optical interferometers and optical thin film; laser and Gaussian beam; polarizer and liquid crystal; solar cell. 
2. Fiber optics and applications Basics of optical fibers; passive and active devices based on optical fibers; their applications in communication, sensing, biomedicine and quantum computing.
課程目標: This course covers the basics and related applications of optoelectronics. The aim is to ignite the interest and imagination of any student who wishes to learn how old stuff such as camera, interferometer and modern stuff such as laser, optical fiber can be put together in a new perspective so that they can be enlightened to pursue their own dreams.

課程概述:
電工實驗（通信專題）是針對電機系三、四年級學生所開設的實作課程。此課程的主要部分包含：
（一）實際操作數位無線通訊主要步驟。
（二）以最新論文為例，評析無線通訊之應用及實驗。
（三）期末專題。

（一）	實際操作數位無線通訊主要步驟
【Week 1 – Week 6：個人MATLAB實驗】
課程學期前六週會使用MATLAB產生以及處理無線通訊訊號，並模擬傳輸及接收。課程涵蓋digital modulation and demodulation, up-sampling and down-sampling, filtering, frequency conversion, synchronization, channel estimation, 以及orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)。同學在前六週使用MATLAB所產生的訊號，以及訊號處理的程序，將在後續課程結合USRP進行實際無線傳輸與接收。

【Week 7 – Week 12：小組USRP實驗】
課程七至十二週會進入USRP操作，觀察常見硬體缺陷對無線通訊的影響，並且傳輸與接收無線訊號。此部分實驗為2-3人一組，同學可自行分組。進入USRP實驗後，課程會有額外由助教帶領的實驗時段，預計會選擇週間的傍晚，實際時段會依修課同學可以參與的時間一起決定。

（二）	無線通訊應用及實驗評析——以最新論文為例
本學期前十二周期間，將透過四次論文評析，從而了解無線通訊網路領域的最新應用，並深入評析其中實驗設計及實驗結果。論文主要從無線領域的頂級會議中選擇，論文會與課程主題相關或是介紹獨特應用。希望透過論文中多樣化的主題，拓展同學們對通信領域的認識，加深基礎操作與應用之間的連結，有助於同學們期末專題的選擇。
論文評析會以「小組辯論」搭配「個人報告」的方式進行，亦即，除了當週負責上台辯論的同學，其他同學都會繳交論文評析的個人報告。辯論分組方式將依據同學的興趣，第一週時會公告所有論文以及對應的課堂辯論日期，同學請依據對主題的興趣填寫志願序，助教將依據同學志願分組，每個同學都需上台辯論一次，正反方由助教隨機安排。

（三）	期末專題
課程之13週至16週為小組期末專題時段，分組延續USRP實驗之小組，應用課程中學習的無線通訊基礎實驗操作，設計實驗探索選定之通信相關題目。專題題目可以是延伸課程中所提及的概念（比如：多天線傳輸與接收），也可以實作特定的應用（比如：感測呼吸）。專題必須包含實作部分，好比說使用MATLAB探索不同信號處理的方式、或是使用USRP做實驗、亦或是使用其他實驗儀器（比如：用喇叭做聲波相關實驗）。期末專題需在期末demo並繳交報告。

開課系所: 工程科學及海洋工程學系 / 工程科學及海洋工程學研究所
課程概述:
本課程介紹有限元素法的理論基礎與計算方法。有限元素法是一種強大的數值分析工具，廣泛應用於工程問題的求解。課程內容涵蓋離散化、元素定式、系統組合、數值解法演算法，以及在結構力學、固體中的熱傳導與聲學頻率及模態分析等應用。

課程主題包括：
1.	導論與回顧
2.	一維元素與計算程序
3.	基本二維元素
4.	變分法
5.	加權殘值法
6.	等參元素
7.	應用：結構動力學與振動、熱傳導、聲學頻率與模態
課程目標:
修習本課程完畢，學生可經由考試、作業、及學期報告來進一步增進下列各項知識技能： 

I. 基礎知識： 
完成本課程後，學生預期能夠：
1.	解釋有限元素法（Finite Element Method, FEM）的理論基礎。
2.	推導並應用一維與二維問題的有限元素定式。
3.	利用解析方法與計算工具建立並求解 FEM 模型。
4.	詮釋與評估 FEM 分析結果，並應用於實際工程問題。
5.	完成並展示一個以工程主題為基礎的 FEM 專題報告。

II. 進階學識： 
除了課堂上吸收的知識，學生更將經由準備作業、考試、及報告各個階段，進而獲得更深入的學理與應用知識。 

III. 獨立作業能力： 
經由整個課程設計，學生將從收集資料、提案、創新思考、及建檔的過程中學習獨立作業能力。 

IV. 思辯能力： 
本項實為研究所學生所需積極培養的能力。經由整個學期學習過程，學生可持續培養綜整文獻與評論的能力，並應用此項思辯能力於創新知識、設計評估科學研究、及評論詮釋研究資料上。 

V. 有效溝通能力： 
經由整個學期口語及書面報告的準備、製作、及呈現，期望進一步培養或增強有效溝通能力

3. 單層複材之巨觀分析 
4. 單層複材之微觀分析 
5. 複合疊層材料之彈性分析 
6. 複合材料之損壞、破壞、及設計

3. 具備線彈性力學的基本知識，了解均向性及異向性材料之差別 
4. 可進行應力、應變、及勁度張量之座標轉換 
5. 具備分析複合疊層材料版之機械特性 
6. 可預測複合疊層材料版之損壞強度 
7. 具備複合材料破壞及性能退化之基本知識 
8. 瞭解近期複合材料的發展與應用

課程概述:
本課程介紹貨幣經濟學的原理和理論。課程涵蓋了貨幣在經濟中的作用、金融市場的運作、利率的決定以及貨幣政策的實施和影響。主要議題包括貨幣供給和需求、通貨膨脹、銀行系統、中央銀行及國際貨幣體系。除此之外，還會補充講解與時事以及各章節相關議題的文章（選自 The Economist, Financial Times, 與各種經濟學文章等）。課程旨在使學生全面了解貨幣因素如何影響經濟表現和政策制定。

課程概述: This course provides an introduction to the principles of modern finance. Specifically, we will be discussing how a corporate manager can evaluate and finance prospective investments and projects. Also, we will talk about how to price various financial instruments, including stocks, bonds, etc. The topics can be broadly divided into the following major areas. The first is called valuation. This part of the course involves learning the concepts and techniques necessary to evaluate the cash flow of projects. A sample of topics covered within this part of the course include time value of money, NPV, internal rate of return, stock prices, bond prices, etc. All of these concepts are used to evaluate projected cash flows of an investment. The second part of the course focuses on the relationship between risk and return. Sample topics include market efficiency, concepts of risk, diversification, portfolio theory, Capital Asset Pricing Model, and behavioral finance. We will also discuss how managers finance the projects after making their investment decisions; this is the issue of capital structure.

1. DCF valuation

This course introduces students to the structure, functions, and risks of financial institutions, with a particular emphasis on the Taiwanese financial industry. Students will learn why financial institutions are “special,” how global financial integration shapes their roles, and how regulatory and institutional frameworks—such as the financial holding company system—have developed in Taiwan. Key risks faced by banks and other financial intermediaries, including interest rate risk, market risk, credit risk, and capital adequacy, will be analyzed. The course also covers deposit insurance and other liability guarantees supporting financial stability.

Through lectures, assignments, group presentations, and discussions, students will not only gain theoretical knowledge but also develop practical skills that are directly relevant to careers in banking, financial regulation, and corporate finance.

3. Examine regulation and policy, including Taiwan’s financial holding company system and deposit insurance, and explain their impact on stability.

4. Apply theoretical concepts to real-world cases in the Taiwanese financial industry.

5. Deliver presentations clearly in English and collaborate effectively in teams.

課程目標:
在人工智慧蓬勃發展的今日，現今大學乃至於統計課程的學習環境也因此劇烈變化；而讓我們能因應這些發展與變化的一個方式，是強化自身的邏輯思考能力。
而高等統計學傳統上為統計學的進階課程，以邏輯論證與推導的方式瞭解統計概念的內涵；在結合上述發展與變化後，一方面本課程將課程目標轉變為：透過統計概念內涵的學習，強化自身的邏輯思考能力。另一方面，本課程在內容上將比傳統高統課花費更多的時間於整合(初等)統計學與高統課的思維，在難度上也將較傳統高統與數理統計學(先修課程對微積分的要求更多(至少8學分或微甲))課程低，但將能使修課同學更易於了解高統與初統兩課程各自的定位，也得以強化對初統的理解。
總之，本課程適合以下三類型同學：1.想強化自身邏輯思考能力的同學、2.想強化統計學中屬於邏輯論證與推導部分學習(但留意本課程難度較傳統高統課略低)的同學、以及3.已修過初統課，但想要再補強初統感覺的同學。(註1, 註2)

EXCEL不僅僅是用來建立表格、製作圖表和彙整資料，財務模型應用更著重於分析。本課程將說明如何在 Excel 中建置財務模型，來協助我們處理財務金問題。
這是一門強調實作學習的課程，您從中學到的技能將對您的職涯非常重要。課程主要使用的軟體是 Excel，我們將利用 Excel 作為解決財務問題的工具。涵蓋的財務主題包括資本預算、財務報表分析、投資組合分析、資本結構、股利政策、債券管理、期權定價與期權交易策略。
課程中會密集使用 Excel 函數和工具，例如 IF、VLOOKUP、INDEX、RAND()、資料表(Data Table)、目標搜尋(Goal Seek)、樞紐分析表(Pivot Table)、目標搜尋(Solver)等。撰寫 VBA 巨集程式也是本課程的重要任務。
完成本課程後，您可以在履歷上寫上「Excel 專家」，並且更有競爭力獲得理想的工作。

課名: 國際金融市場暨財務管理
開課系所: 財務金融學系 / 財務金融學研究所
課程概述: 川普政府對全球發動關稅戰帶來高度不確定性，美元與美債一度失去過去的避險地位，進一步引爆匯率戰與貨幣戰。台灣作為出口導向的經濟體，所受衝擊尤為明顯，例如今年截至6月5日，新台幣兌美元升值已近10%，對出口產業造成實質衝擊。本課程將討論如何因應匯率的劇烈波動，以及企業或個人應如何調整財務策略與風險管理手段來降低風險，並進一步探討「美元霸權」的未來。尤其是探討2025年7月17日美國「天才法案」通過後，穩定幣對美債及美元的影響。下半學期，我們將介紹如何運用在前半學期所學到的知識，來制定有效的國際金融市場投資策略；這部分的內容將涵蓋對貨幣、債券和股票的投資策略。
課程目標:
本課程會討論的問題如下：
1.	匯率是如何影響國際金融市場上的投資行為？
2.	如何透過即期及遠期匯率資訊解讀市場對某國貨幣在未來，相對於美元是看升或看貶？
3.	如何使用各項財務工具（例如：遠期外匯、期貨及選擇權）來降低匯率風險，以及長期投資策略上是否應利用海外直接投資（FDI）避險。
4.	探討美國雙赤字帶來的衝擊、Bretton Woods至今美元地位的基本支撐，以及從黃金、SDR與穩定幣看美元。

本課程著重實務上的應用，利用課堂中所學，解讀國際金融市場變化的意涵。若同學對以上所介紹的課程有興趣，歡迎選修本課程。

	THIS COURSE IS DEVOTED TO A STUDY OF FIXED INCOME SECURITIES AND DERIVATIVES IN TAIWAN, U.S. AND THE OTHER.  IT IS CONCERNED WITH THE MARKETS (INCLUDING THE UNDERGROUND MARKETS), INSTITUTIONS, LAWS, REGULATIONS, AND TECHNIQUES THROUGH WHICH BONDS AND OTHER SECURITIES ARE TRADED, INTEREST RATES DETERMINED, AND FINANCIAL SERVICES PRODUCED AND DELIVERED. I DESIGN THIS COURSE WITH THE THREE PURPOSES: (1) TO ARM YOU WITH ANALYTICAL TOOLS TO HELP YOU UNDERSTAND WHY THE FINANCIAL MARKETPLACE BEHAVES AS IT DOES AND HOW WE SHOULD MAKE FINANCIAL DECISIONS; (2) TO DESCRIBE HOW TODAY’S FINANCIAL MARKETS OPERATE AND WHERE THEY APPEAR TO BE HEADED; (3) TO UNDERSTAND WHAT DIFFERENCES BETWEEN OUR MARKETS AND U. S. MARKETS ARE AND HOW YOU ADJUST YOUR FINANCIAL DECISIONS GIVEN DIFFERENT MARKETS IN TWO COUNTRIES, SO THAT YOU CAN MORE EASILY “SPEAK THE LANGUAGE” OF THE MARKETS AND FIND YOUR WAY AROUND IN THEM.
	FIXED INCOME SECURITIES AND DERIVATIVES ARE A FASCINATING FIELD OF STUDY. WHAT HAPPENS IN THESE MARKETS AFFECTS THE QUALITY OF OUR LIVES EVERY DAY IN MANY DIFFERENT WAYS. MOREOVER, THESE FINANCIAL MARKETS ARE DYNAMIC INSTITUTIONS CONTINUALLY ”PUTTING ON A NEW FACE” IN THE FORM OF NEW SERVICES, NEW INSTRUMENTS, AND NEW METHODS. THUS, THERE ARE ABUNDANT MATERIALS DESERVED TO BE STUDIED. DUE TO THE LIMITED TIME, HOWEVER, THIS COURSE PROVIDES ONLY THE FUNDAMENTAL INTRODUCTION TO THESE VAST, EVER-CHANGING MARKETS. TO THOSE WANT TO BUILD THEIR CAREER UPON THIS AREA, THEY SHOULD STRENGTHEN THEIR KNOWLEDGE IN THIS AREA THROUGH CONTINUED READING AND PERSONAL INVOLVEMENT, E.G, WRITING A THESIS.

THIS COURSE WILL GIVE STUDENTS NOT ONLY THE ANALYTICAL TOOLS BUT ALSO THE LANGUAGE OF THE FINANCIAL MARKETS BECAUSE IN FINANCIAL MARKETS PEOPLE DEVELOP SPECIAL TERMS OR GIVE COMMON TERMS SPECIAL MEANINGS IN ORDER TO BEING ABLE TO COMMUNICATE PRECISELY AND RAPIDLY WITH EACH OTHER. 近年來公司財務管理、銀行資產負債管理、投信基金管理、保險公司資產負債管理、新金融商品設計、以及各類金融商品的投資理財等財務金融領域快速發展與演進，造就了「財務工程」這門新學科。「財務工程」由於興起時間很短，因此它的內容尚未完全界定清楚，在財務金融不同領域工作的人，對「財務工程」的說法就不同，但總括來說「財務工程」大概包含下列之內容：它是用以解決財務金融問題的一種過程、及設計財務金融產品解決問題的技術。更具體的說它包含界定問題、設計商品、組合或分解技術、商品定價與避險、商品推廣、商品通路的建立等，都是「財務工程」的範疇。
由上述對「財務工程」的定義可知，「財務工程」其實不單只是設計新的金融商品或是對新金融商品評價而已，而應是包含上自界定問題、下至推廣與配銷都是一貫要思考與解決的問題，缺少其中任何一個環節都不是完美的「財務工程」，也都無法真正解決所面臨的財務金融問題。因此，本課程雖名為「金融創新」，但不以只介紹或設計新金融商品、或是只對新金融商品評價為目標而已，而是要探討令新金融商品成功之「財務工程」的各個步驟與環節，讓學員「見樹又見林」的了解「金融創新」的真義，而非僅是了解「金融創新」的片段。
	本課程每週授課一次，授課內容如下所示。授課內容以已在臺灣盛行之新金融商品為主要探討標的，主要探討其發行原因、動機、目的、及未來發展的前景，當然該新金融商品整個的「財務工程」亦將詳細討論。除了介紹臺灣已盛行之新金融商品外，本課程亦要探討最近的將來最可能引進臺灣的新金融商品。當然介紹各種新金融商品之前，需要的財務理論與評價技巧亦是本課程討論的重點之一。
如眾所周知的，學習「金融創新」或「財務工程」是需要許多財務理論、計量技巧、與電腦技術的，學員能從本課程獲得多少專業知識，其實和你的投入時間與你有前面提到的知識多寡有絕對的關係。不過學員不必焦慮或緊張，本課程將會把財務理論、計量技巧、與電腦技術的份量盡可能的降到最低，以利大多數人的學習。至於程度高者，可自行學習、自我挑戰。本課程有多次不定期的作業，以利學員練習；一次期末考試。本課程鼓勵學員發問問題、提出時事或個案於課堂上討論。你的成績與期末考試分數及課堂上的表現成正相關。本課程將會不定期發放講義，沒有上課教科書，但是下面這一本參考書值得你擁有。

課程概述:
This is the first course in econometrics for Master students and aims to prepare students for real world data analysis. In the first part of course, we will introduce 3 leading econometric methods that are applicable to different model structures: the ordinary least squares (OLS) method, the instrumental variable (IV) method, and the maximum likelihood (ML) method. As an extension of the IV method, we will cover briefly the generalized method of moment (GMM). Some computational methods, such as bootstrap and LASSO, that help improve conventional methods will also be discussed. In the second part of this course, we will go beyond linear models and introduce some statistical learning methods, including classification and regression trees, random forests, bagging, and boosting. I will follow my own lecture slides ([M1] below); see textbooks [M2] & [M3] for more details. Readings [S1], [S2], & [S3] are useful supplements for some lectures; [S2] is particularly helpful if you are interested in econometric theory.
This course requires knowledge in probability theory, multivariate statistics, linear/matrix algebra, and (stochastic) convergence concepts. Undergraduate students with proper mathematical background are welcome to take this course. All students are required to learn coding in R, a common programming tool. There will be weekly homework assignments, including analytical and computational exercises. Your grade will be determined by homework, a midterm exam, and a final exam.

課程概述: 後基因體和蛋白體時代，更受到重視的是所謂的"表現型"，而代謝物 (metabolites) 即是基因最終的表現產物。我們都知道，生物體有相關的基因，不見得會表現出相關的化合物，或說不確定表現量為如何? 因此，本課程主要介紹分析代謝物的儀器種類和技術，如: HPLC、CE、NMR、MS等，以及如何獲取合格的圖譜與該如何判讀。
課程目標: 本課程涵括目前常用於分析各種生物體中一級和二級代謝物的方法，希望學生在進行生理、生化和各種指標化合物之定性與定量相關研究時，能夠了解哪種設備可提供何種資訊，進而找到解決問題方法，最後得以順利完成其研究。
課程要求: 希望同學具有普通化學的基本概念。

課名: 計量生態與水產資源專題討論
課程概述: 自然系統的資源管理經常需涉及對系統內組成的分布和動態進行定量化的描述和推論。本門課程是針對在生態學、水產資源學、生物資訊學、動態系統方面具有基礎理解的學生所設計的。它旨在探討如何透過計量方法和建模以解決漁業生態與資源管理中的問題之應用。此外，本課程還涵蓋了當代計量生物學常使用的演算法之介紹。學生透過閱讀和生態學與水產資源學相關的經典書籍，選擇個人感興趣的主題並就此展示的學習進展。課堂主要以互動式討論為主。

課程概述: The first semester of Freshman English focuses on improving students’ fluency and accuracy in language reception and production especially in the listening and speaking skill areas. Attentive listening is a critical skill that students must master in order to carry out meaningful conversations for the purpose of effective communication. Knowing that some students in their first semester at the university are not accustomed to speaking in English, the instructor will first build up students’ confidence through in-class listening and speaking activities of familiar topics. Once students feel comfortable speaking up in such controlled class setting, they will then be guided to speak on more challenging topics and even debate with each other. Students will also develop proper writing habits while writing compositions using the “preferable” writing approach. Listening, speaking, reading, and writing are valuable skills students need to be equipped with in order to continue with their college work throughout their university lives.
課程目標: One main goal of this course is to help students bridge the gap between high school English and college English. Under the instructor’s guidance, it is with hope that students can make use of their already well-learned grammar and vocabulary to orally express themselves clearly and effectively and to produce well-planned writing assignments at the college level. Through involving in oral discussions and writing compositions on various topics, global and local, students will be exposed to different kinds of knowledge necessary for developing critical thinking and academic skills. Mastering these skills, along with English skills, ensures students a smooth transition to taking EMI courses.
課程要求:
This course is conducted entirely in English. Students are required to speak to their peers and instructor in English in the classroom. Since students only meet with the instructor once a week for 3 hours, students are expected to take an active role in all class activities to maximize their learning opportunities. A student-centered approach will be adopted to allow students to make full use of class time to achieve their English-learning goals and course learning objectives. Students who are not serious in their learning please do not consider signing up for this course.

Students should come to class on time and prepared. Students who “need” to be late or absent should notify the instructor via email with a valid reason at least 2 days in advance. Students must submit all three compositions. Late work will NOT be accepted. Students missing 2 or more class meetings automatically fail the course. Students who do not complete WalkyTalky and/or Freshman Shorts are not allowed to pass the course.

Cell phones and other electronic devices are not allowed to be used in class unless given permission by the instructor to do so.

Course Description:
This course intends to provide guidelines for first-year students to smoothly
adapt to English-speaking environment. As English has become a lingua franca
after the end of the Cold War in the late 1980s and early 1990s, this FYE course
adopts a theme-based approach to guide students into diverse and meaningful
English discussions in order to prepare for future participation in conversations
with international communities. The course aims to close-read canonized and
nonfictional western short fictions, editorial essays, and stories. Multiple
audio-visual supplementary materials will be provided to enhance
understandings in four-sills English learning. Together we will learn to read with
care and will review literary history as well as social-political background,
especially the impact on how English texts are been written and reviewed; how
English writing can be a kind of artistic, intellectual, as well as inspirational
productions. Meanwhile, the aim is to possess a good command of English and
comprehensive knowledge of the great body of knowledge written in the western
world. Thus, to enrich our understanding of its culture and history of idea. That
is, in our selected readings and discussion, we will be concerned with individual
thoughts and works in terms of the whole western cultural context.
課程目標:
Course Objectives:
1. This course deals with western texts written in English as an essential key to
learn English.
2. Students will be required to discuss in professional ESP (English for Special
Purpose) and EAP (English for Academic Purpose) terms.
3. General background ideas about western cultures and
multilingual/multicultural texts in English will be provided and lectured so as
to assist further understanding of these required readings.
課程要求:
Requirements:
Enjoy learning English while using English to approach this world with
intellectual perspectives. The students will be encouraged to develop a love of
acquiring English to explore western cultures, languages, and literatures as a
foundation for creatively and professionally becoming world citizens.

課程概述:
The purpose of learning English is to use it and to have fun!

This course is dedicated to creating an interactive environment for students to use English to think, communicate, reflect, and most importantly, to develop critical thinking abilities with academic rigor. The four skills in English—listening, reading, writing, and speaking—will be effectively integrated throughout this semester. Each session contains listening and reading practices as well as various in-class activities, such as peer collaboration, group discussions, presentations, writing workshop, and interactive games. In particular, students are expected to regularly contribute to English-only class discussions. Reading handouts will be available on the NTU COOL site.

Meanwhile, English conversation practice is highlighted through numerous discussion-based activities. By the end of this course during the fall semester, students are expected to demonstrate proficiency in English through expanding their knowledge and perspectives on various subjects from authentic English materials.

It also aims to cultivate students’ fundamental core abilities and prepare them for future EMI (English as a Medium of Instruction) courses. A variety of task-based activities and communicative activities and exercises, such as class discussions, dialogues, role plays, essay writing, and speeches, are designed to motivate students to speak confidently and help them acquire greater fluency in spoken English. 課程概述:
This course is intended to help students develop critical thinking and effective reading strategies. In order to accomplish this, teamwork, cultural study, and practical language skills are emphasised as the course progresses. The sessions in this semester will focus on the following areas: (1) active reading skills; (2) presentation skills and group work; (3) critical thinking. A wide range of reading and multi-media materials are selected to associate language learning with the students’ daily life, personal development, as well as their knowledge about the latest development in culture, science, entertainment, news, etc. Information about English spoken outside USA will also be introduced, so as to broaden students’ worldview. In addition, the students will be provided with readings about how to be a happy and successful individual in their college life. 

The course aims to balance lectures with classroom activities, which include group discussion and presentation, film viewing and critique, performance, Q&A, report writing, and occasionally language games. With guidance from the instructor, the students will learn essential language and social skills by completing various tasks. Given the focus on communication and interaction, students’ participation in discussion and activities is crucial, and the atmosphere in the classroom is expected to be relaxing yet intellectually stimulating. 

◎Please note that this course will be taught in English.

This course aims to enhance students’ integrated skills in English listening, speaking, reading, and writing, while fostering their capacity for autonomous and cooperative learning. It is specifically designed for motivated learners who are strongly committed to improving their English proficiency.

The course adopts a student-centered approach to inspire self-directed learning. With guidance, students will apply language learning strategies and utilize audio-visual materials and online resources to practice the four skills individually, in pairs, or in small groups.

The course also encourages students to extend their learning beyond the classroom by leveraging online and campus resources, planning independent learning, and completing personal English learning activities or projects.

*For details of the course, please visit the course website: http://eltrlab.fll.ntu.edu.tw/.
課程目標:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

課程要求:
1. First-Week Attendance
Students must attend the first week of classes to confirm enrollment. Those unable to attend must apply for leave in advance. Attendance will be taken during the first week, and unexcused absences will result in automatic withdrawal from the course.

2. Technology and Time Commitment
This course is designed for students willing to use computers and the Internet for coursework. In addition to the three hours of weekly class time, students are expected to dedicate an equivalent amount of time to previewing and reviewing materials.

3. Attendance and Participation
Students must attend class on time, be fully prepared, and actively participate in group discussions and classroom activities to maximize learning outcomes. Latecomers must report their arrival, and those needing to leave early or apply for leave must notify the instructor in advance to avoid being marked absent.

4. Course Evaluation
Assessment includes diverse listening, speaking, reading, and writing evaluations, emphasizing regular class participation, in-class practice, quizzes, and assignments. Students with approved absences must complete any missed tests or assignments within one week, with scores capped at 80%. Failure to meet this deadline or submission of plagiarized work will result in a score of zero. Cheating during exams will be handled according to university regulations.

5. Leave Policies
Students who miss class must use the NTU Online Leave Request System to apply for leave. Unapproved absences or exceeding the allowed leave period will be treated as truancy. Missing one hour of class is equivalent to five hours of leave. Unexcused absences exceeding one-third of the total course hours will result in a failing grade, recorded as an "X" grade (refer to Chapter 4 of the NTU Academic Regulations).

6. Oral Presentations
Details of oral presentations will be discussed during class.

7. Course Website
Students must check the course website (ELTRLab) weekly for updates, announcements, and important information.

課程概述:
This class is an introduction of basic toolkits for appreciating literary works. In this first required class in the program, the students will learn how to analyze the style of literary language, dissect the narrative construction of a story, and reflect upon the use of symbolic language and thematic reverberances in fiction. We will also move through different genres: short stories, poems, and plays. As you will find out, this is no easy task. For one thing, you are asked to perceive language differently: not simply as a transparent medium through which one is able to communicate with other people, but as a delicately refractive—though resolutely conventional—layer that appeals to our intellectual capacity and poetic imagination. This is, to wit, the task of reading. We are going to see how English grammar, something we all learned in high school as a set of unbreakable rules, becomes quite malleable in the hands of these great writers. Passing through that malleability would enable us to think about the porous relationship between ordinary and literary languages. In the meantime, I would bring in various film examples to illustrate how certain concepts are able to migrate to another medium and provide equally powerful tools for narrative analysis.
	
Each session will proceed as follows: I’ll spend the several 15–20-minute lectures about the materials and ask impromptu questions—which is the time for you to impress me. In between, I will provide some discussion questions on the slides. You should find some friends of yours and one new member to make up your discussion group of five to six people. The length of the discussion will be about 20 minutes. Then we’ll spend 10 minutes going through some tentative answers as provided by each of you. In the last 20 minutes of the class, I will provide another lecture to wrap things up.
課程目標:
Attendance and Participation (20%):
Teaching assistants will be responsible for taking your attendance. Please report to them after class to make sure your presence is noted. You are allowed one unexcused absences for this class. Every absence after the one allowed will hurt your attendance grade gravely. In every class, we will have an active discussion about the text for an hour. If you see something, say something.  When answering a question, speak your name first and this is how we score your attendance. 

Two Assignments and Two Short Papers (40%):
For the first assignment, you will be given a list of grammatical terms and two pages of fiction that we are going to read together in class. Your task is to mark every grammatical usage in these two pages according to the lexicon provided. For example, if I list “absolute phrases” in the lexicon, then you will need to pick out every absolute phrase in the excerpt. This is an exercise to train your perception of stylistic distinctions through grammatical maneuvers.

The second assignment, “De-Modernize Faulkner,” is to train you in reading difficult texts. What you need to do is to fill in the blanks left by the text and translate the author’s stylistic narration into plain English. In the process, you’ll figure out where the ambiguities lie and understand the task of reading. 

For the two two-page papers, you are required to pick up one sentence in the text we are supposed to read that week and provide an analysis of why it is important by itself, in the paragraph, in the section, or/and in the overall organization of the narrative. We will be doing all of these assignments IN CLASS.

I want a precise, analytical prose that employs grammatical terms to clarify the intricacies of the writer’s language. No impressionistic or self-indulgent reading is allowed. Do not say “I feel,” “I like,” “I am impressed,” etc. Nobody cares. Be persuasive and convincing without resorting to sentimentalizing tidbits. For collocation, use https://www.english-corpora.org/coca/ There are a lot of useful online dictionaries and thesauruses. Common grammatical errors will hurt your grade, very much. Consider proofreading. 

Midterm (15%), Final Exam (25%): 
Multiple-choice questions (Taiwanese students’ favorite), identifications (two sentences), short answer questions (one paragraph), and essay questions. A review of the materials covered will be provided prior to the exams.

Course Description: 

This course begins with an introduction to ancient Near Eastern literature and then continues to discuss the Hebrew Bible to explore the ancient Hebrew culture and the relationship between man and God. Then we enter the world of Greek Mythology by reading Homer’s epics: Iliad and Odyssey. Following the Trojan legend, we read Virgil’s Aeneid to explore how the Romans created their national epic based on the story of Troy. Each of these works is read closely, analyzed carefully, and discussed with its own cultural and historical context. Close reading for literary analysis is emphasized in class. We will proceed in the following forms: lectures, group discussions, and video-watching before class. Before class, students are expected to finish reading materials and watch videos. After class, students need to post a response on the forum on the course website. At the beginning of each class, we will have a 5-minute quiz. Finally, students must give a short oral group presentation (about 10 minutes) in class. 

For the group presentations, students need to send their PPT slides to the instructor and the TAs at least one week before the presentation date. 

Participation in the first week’s class is necessary for students to ensure their enrollment in this class. Reading materials for the first week’s class will be sent to students one week before school starts. If one is interested in taking this course and wishes to get the reading materials for the first week, please email the instructor. Due to the classroom capacity, there is no guarantee that students who are not automatically registered in this course may enroll successfully. This course does not accept auditors.

This course is designed as a survey course that encompasses significant prose and poetry of western writers from ancient Near Eastern literature to Virgil’s Aeneid. By focusing on these canonical works, this course aims to lead students to explore the beginning of human civilization, ancient cultures, and important classical legends. At the end of the course, students will be able to:
1. Understand important ideas in ancient, classical, and medieval literature and cultures.
2. Analyze important themes and motives in these literary works.
3. Get familiar with the Hebrew, Greek, and Roman traditions.

2. Weekly quizzes

課程概述:
Writing is difficult. Some people believe that good writers are born that way, that they have a natural gift. My goal in this course is to fight this notion. Instead, I will argue that effective written communication can be mastered once we break it down into specific skills and tasks. In other words, writing is difficult precisely because it is a process involving several steps, from planning and organizing a text’s content (catchy introductions, clear outline, original thinking) to crafting its form (word choices, sentence structures, paragraph transitions). In this course, I will familiarize you with these and related techniques. We will discuss a wide range of textual and audiovisual materials. I have selected these as models that will inspire and help you get started as a writer. You will learn by reading and watching these materials, but, first and foremost, you will learn by practicing writing. In addition to impromptu exercises, you will produce six formal writing assignments. These, together with in-class quizzes and overall participation will be the foundation of your final grade.

課程概述: The rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence is spurring change in all industry workforces and revolutionizing the ways we do business. It is therefore imperative that students and teachers re-examine the conceptualization and practice of “training” in this new context. Core questions this course aims to tackle: What distinguishes a “good” speaker from a “bad” one? Can we use technology to our advantage to achieve our communication goals? In this course, we will explore possible answers by first establishing what you (the speaker) want to say about a specific topic, what your intentions are. Then, with the aid of technology, polish your thoughts, script, and speech. Assessment of whether or not your message came across—or whether a dialogue can ensue—will fall to the interpretation of what you said by your peers and/or the instructor.
課程目標:
Achieving communication goals in the context of this course refers to speakers being able to:
•	Express intended meaning: logic, cohesion, coherence 
•	Use idiomatic/“standard” language: word choice, grammar, collocation, connotation, register
•	Engage in fluent delivery: pacing, prosody, pronunciation, enunciation, intonation, confidence, voice
Primary ways to achieve the above goals:
•	Research parallel texts to identify idiomatic/ “standard” language for a given topic or your intended meaning
•	Use technology to aid in producing speech that exhibits “native” speech qualities; these technologies include (but are not limited to):
o	Grammarly
o	ChatGPT
o	Speech-to-text or text-to-speech apps (Natural Reader, NOA)
o	Online video resources (YouTube)

Course Description 
The main goals of this course are :
     (1) to teach you more effective listening skills – this will be done mainly through assigned audio and video file-based listening and transcription exercises, and daily independent echo practice; and 
     (2) to improve your pronunciation, starting from cognitive understanding of the mechanics of pronunciation, to daily practice to solidify and fully automate the correct forms, to class performances of scenes from television series. 

*This course is elective, but strongly recommended for incoming DFLL freshmen who scored 70% or less on the Pronunciation Placement Test given in early September. Other DFLL students, including department minors and double majors, are welcome as well. Non-DFLL students and auditors will not be admitted except under special circumstances, with the instructor's permission.
課程目標:
Course Objectives 
     Languages are best learned through listening and imitating good models of the spoken language. A major weakness in English education in Taiwan is an emphasis on grammar learning through rules, vocabulary learning from a printed page, in which the learner guesses at the correct sound, and a corresponding lack of practice listening to and imitating good audio models. 
     This class will attempt to help fill in this gap by giving students guidance in how to listen, how to pronounce accurately, and how to learn and continue learning independently through life. Emphasis will be placed on cultivating active new habits to overwrite previous faulty, passive ones.

課程概述:
Composition II is a year-long course that focuses on writing full-length essays. To set the foundation for academic writing, four important skills – summarizing, evaluating, synthesizing, and arguing – will be closely examined, discussed, and put into practice in the first semester (you will also have the opportunity to explore how these skills are embedded in professions that involve plenty of writing). The course will be delivered in a range of formats, including in-class discussions, writing workshops, and individual/pair supervisions, all of which require your active participation.

In the first semester, teaching will be done in a "flipped" approach, which means that you will be asked to complete all assigned readings **before class**. When we meet in person, class time will be arranged as the following: 1) pre-writing discussion (on the assigned reading material), 2) writing (without the use of any technological devices), and 3) post-writing discussion (reflection and analysis). In the second semester, we will dive deeper into a set of topics in the arts, humanities, and social sciences by incorporating in-class debates into pre-writing discussions. Additionally, we will incorporate the use of AI-assisted technologies into our writing routine and critically examine the role of AI in the production of text, discourse, and knowledge.

Note:
- This course will be primarily conducted in English.
- Referencing in all course assignments will follow APA style.
課程目標:
By the end of the first semester, you will:
- Be more confident in engaging with – and responding to – different academic texts.
- Develop skills in summarizing, evaluating, synthesizing, and arguing.
- Be able to apply these skills in writing full-length essays.
- Expand your understanding about the role of these skills in different types of professions that involve writing.

Interview presentation

Many jobs require one to write. Of course, writing in different professions may look quite different: it could be as simple as writing short notes on standardized forms; it could be as complex as writing research papers, controversial issues, literary pieces, or project proposals and reports. For this assignment, you are asked, in groups of three, to interview someone whose job requires regular and extensive writing **primarily in English**.
